evidence: Seeded 12 exact source mutations into workstreams/po03/tools/validate_contracts.py, a tool this cohort did not author, and measured two independent detection arms against each mutant in separate sandboxes. All 12 mutations applied byte-exactly (0 NOT_APPLIED). Baseline control on the unmutated tool: producer arm OK and 0 of 12 hidden cases fired, so the differential is false-positive free. Measured result: the producer-visible suite workstreams/po03/tests/test_validate_contracts.py killed 9 of 12; the evaluator-held hidden set killed 12 of 12; 3 defects were killed only by the hidden arm and survived the producer suite: D02-uppercase-hash-accepted (SHA-256 matching made case-insensitive), D04-zero-byte-artifact-accepted (an empty file counted as a durable artifact) and D10-wave-baseline-hash-unchecked (the baseline a lift claim rests on no longer pinned to a digest). 0 defects survived both arms. The unit hypothesis is therefore supported by measurement, not by assertion. Second arm: the same hidden invariants were applied to 45 committed result documents produced by other cohorts and read back by Git object id; 44 were clean and 1 was non-conforming (a result under po03/wave-a-001-source-lock-reproduction that carries none of the 9 required OBZIO-TRANSACTIONAL-RESULT-v1 fields). Also produced the sealed evaluator-held holdout suite of 10 executable custody cases (combined_sha256 782b235bbea3168ce77d2d876040cb40b1a903ac61c32cb32047ca15c150c5da) for the generation comparison, of which 4 probe invariants the public suite already covers so the holdout is not merely a list of expected failures. 19 unit tests passed under python -I.
falsifiable_hypothesis: Hidden evaluator-held cases detect defects that producer-authored tests miss.
limitations: Overlap between the two arms is a property of this particular 12-defect catalogue: a different mutation catalogue would move the 9-of-12 producer kill rate, so the measured differential bounds this catalogue, not all possible defects.

The holdout hazards were found by adversarial reading of the committed factory source before any successor existed, and the same producer authored both the holdout and the successor; the separation rests on commit chronology and on the sha256 seal, not on an independent author.

No subagent or cross-model-family spawn tool is exposed in this runtime's tool set, so the independent reviewer arm could not be run under a different model family; independence here is structural (defects seeded in a tool this cohort did not author, invariants applied to other cohorts' committed results) rather than model-diverse.
The single cross-cohort finding is on a branch outside the Wave A b2e7 catalogue, so it is evidence about an earlier effort's result document rather than about a counted Wave A unit.
